title: Mesoscopic local pointed Gromov-Hausdorff limits of sparse planar and unicellular maps through tilted bipointed CRT edge decoration
difficulty_reason: Allow the existing exact core-kernel enumeration/contraction/factorial-tail framework, its all-sparse relative-concentration support, standard local CLT and invariance principles, Brownian excursion/CRT coding and Bismut decomposition. The remaining model construction couples the root-marked finite forest to independently tilted bipointed CRT edge blocks jointly with random positive-partition chain lengths, identifies the root tree with the dangling-leaf decoration, and passes from a fixed kernel ball to a metric ball through a no-shortcut localization bound. These joint marked-tree and quotient-metric constructions retain one H2 core. Bridge density/Stirling calculations, named Bismut tools and the crude path deviation estimate do not separately justify H3; root-volume and smaller tree-scale companions are support or the same mechanism, not extra cores.

problems.title: Poisson kernel-defect limit for sparse uniform planar or unicellular rooted maps at a finite cubic sparsity crossover
problems.difficulty_reason: A pointwise enumeration ratio is insufficient to determine the defect law because mass could escape through arbitrarily large defects. Sections2–3 prove the exact core-kernel enumeration and uniform near-trivalent contraction ratios, transferring loop controls through Catalan-weighted forests. Section4 combines those new estimates with a uniform factorial tail to normalize the finite-crossover Poisson law, so its difficulty is not the final ratio-to-Poisson calculation alone.

problems.title: Annealed multifractal exponents of the leaf-growth measure on uniform plane binary trees
problems.difficulty_reason: The prior uniform leaf-growth construction and Catalan estimates leave all real-power moments and their exponent unresolved, especially for negative powers at the singular endpoints. The authors derive the exact two-subtree moment recurrence and build upper/lower inductive comparison barriers controlled by the sign of an improper integral. The new uniform endpoint estimates, including separate bounds valid independently of the signs of the powers, justify the required dominated limit and identify the unique exponent throughout its stated parameter domain.

The main conditioned-tree conclusion additionally requires the explicit three-piece comparison and a locality argument absorbing both upper fluxes into empty lower-spine spots. Those source-local coupled constructions and limit controls are nonroutine, so the full theorem is conservatively H1.

actual_statement_excerpts.statement:
\begin{lemma} \label{extension} Fix three dimensions $1 \le d \le m < n$ and let $Y$ be a $d$-dimensional simplicial complex with at most $V$ vertices, so that each vertex lies in at most $D$ simplices. Suppose that for some $R>0$ we have a map,
		$$f: Y(d-1) \to [0, R]^{n-1} \times \{0\} \subset \RR^{n}$$
		
		\noindent which is $(m-1)$-sparse with overlap $S$. Then there is an extension of $f$,
		
		$$F: Y \to [0, R]^n  \subset \RR^{n}$$
		
		\noindent which is $m$-sparse with overlap $S'(n,D,S)$, where $S'(n,D,S)$ only depends on $n, D$ and $S$.
	\end{lemma}
